solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post, which drops the counts, so each count is read off the blogger's answer

clue.text: Vacuous cove with valet eagerly pursues soak westwards

indicators.note: in an across answer, travelling west means reading from right to left

blocks.note: to woo is to court or pursue with ardour
to ret is to soak flax or hemp to soften it

explanation.surface: A dim fellow with a manservant goes keenly after a drunkard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soak' looks like a drunk, but it is the verb ret, turned round to TER. Bertie Wooster is P.G. Wodehouse's amiable dimwit, looked after by his valet Jeeves.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertie Wooster, the brainless gentleman of Wodehouse's comic novels, is famously rescued from scrapes by his valet Jeeves.

clue.text: You can't replace this wife since a setting's set (12, two words)

indicators.note: to set something is to arrange or compose it, so the letters before it are put in a new order

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife
as in 'as it rained, we stayed in'
taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A setter boasts that a wife is irreplaceable because the arrangement is fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase describing the answer: a wasting asset wears away and is not renewed.
explanation.definitionFit: In accounting a wasting asset is property such as a mine or lease whose value is used up over time and cannot be restored.

clue.text: Solution which damages floor surface, three top bits scratched

indicators.note: in a down answer the top is the start, so its first three letters are struck off

blocks.note: a hard-wearing sheet flooring

explanation.surface: A cleaning fluid that harms a floor has scraped off its upper layers.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'solution' is a chemical one, not an answer to a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleum is fuming sulphuric acid, a corrosive liquid solution of sulphur trioxide that attacks most materials.

clue.text: Scots stew containing their own cocaine stand-by

indicators.note: containing means one word holds the other inside it

blocks.note: in Scots, to stove is to stew
ain is Scots for own, so the Scots' own word

explanation.surface: A Scottish stew includes the locals' own home-grown substitute for a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Their own' carries over the Scots from 'Scots stew': the word for own in their dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Stovaine was a synthetic local anaesthetic introduced as a less toxic substitute for cocaine.

clue.text: Zola, for example, in English middle-distance race

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
the mile is a classic middle-distance event

explanation.surface: A French novelist apparently entered an English running race.
explanation.definitionFit: Zola's first name was Émile, so he is one example of a person called Emile.

clue.text: Dramatically oppose old fox in early run

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

blocks.note: ren is an obsolete form of run
pug is an old name for a fox

explanation.surface: An actor resists an aged fox that runs early in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dramatically' marks the word as Shakespearean or theatrical in use.
explanation.definitionFit: Repugn is an archaic verb meaning to resist or fight against, found in Shakespeare's plays.

clue.text: Downright eccentricity

blocks.note: first meaning: utter, absolute, as in nonsense of the purest kind
second meaning: a deviation or swerve from a set course

explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentricity' looks like oddness of character; here it is the geometric sense of departing from a centre or line.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for utter and also a noun for a ship's swerve or deviation off course.

clue.text: Sludgy and cold brash old boy tucking into rasher (7, two words)

indicators.note: tucking into means one piece is placed snugly inside the other

blocks.note: a rasher is a slice of bacon
OB is the abbreviation for old boy

explanation.surface: A bold old schoolfellow, cold and slurring, digs into some bacon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brash' looks like an adjective for the old boy, but it is a noun: a mass of broken floating ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Slob ice is a sludgy mass of floating ice crystals, a kind of brash, the broken ice found at sea.

clue.text: We must look up that expression of regret used by Rab C

definitions.text: expression of regret used by Rab C

indicators.note: in a down answer, looking up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
how can stand for that, as in 'he told me how he was ill'

explanation.surface: A Glaswegian has to search for a phrase of sorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: Rab C Nesbitt is a Glaswegian comedy character, so the word is Scots: ewhow is a Scots cry of alas.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewhow is a Scots interjection of grief or regret, the kind Glasgow's Rab C Nesbitt might use.

clue.text: Crude oil is gunge — it gets you making plugs

indicators.note: crude means rough and unrefined, so the letters are in a raw jumbled order

blocks.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Raw oil turns to sludge, which is good for filling holes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plugs' looks like stoppers for holes; it is the informal verb for promoting something.
explanation.definitionFit: To plug a product is to praise it publicly, and eulogising is praising highly.

clue.text: Dashed mad theory involving the plague? (12, three words)

indicators.note: dashed means smashed to pieces, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crazy hypothesis about the Black Death has been ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a loose definition: pestering someone with endless verse is a kind of plaguing. Old Irish lore held that rats could be killed by rhyming.
explanation.definitionFit: To rhyme to death is to torment someone with verses, and so to harass or pester them.

clue.text: Well, I'm struggling with a lot — it's as bad as it gets (10, two words)

definitions.text: it's as bad as it gets

indicators.note: struggling suggests writhing and twisting, so the letters are thrown about

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sighs that they are battling a heavy burden and could not feel worse.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-time low is the worst level ever reached, the bottom point of a record.

clue.text: Find tomb by taking little edition out of trunks

indicators.note: taking something out of a word means removing those letters from it

blocks.note: Speedos are a brand of swimming trunks
ed. is the short form of edition

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a grave by pulling a small book out of a pair of chests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunks' suggests storage chests; it means swimwear here.
explanation.definitionFit: A speos is an ancient Egyptian temple or tomb cut out of the solid rock.

clue.text: Quiet drink? Duck into misplaced glory for creed of sin

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside the other
misplaced means put in the wrong position, so the letters are shifted about

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly
as in 'have one with me', a single drink
taken as written
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A quiet tipple, then a hunter takes cover in some faded fame to become a doctrine of wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Ponerology is the branch of theology dealing with the doctrine of evil, from Greek poneros, wicked.

clue.text: Daughter sliced bread getting into fold like the upper class do

indicators.note: sliced means cut off, so the daughter's letter is lopped from the word
getting into means the piece goes inside another

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
bread and dosh are both slang for money
a ply is a fold or layer

explanation.surface: A girl cuts a loaf and puts it in a sheep pen, as gentry would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for money here, not a loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Poshly is an adverb for behaving in a smart, upper-class manner.

clue.text: Inkling to oust Earl and clear a lounge in the Athenaeum, say

definitions.text: a lounge in the Athenaeum, say

indicators.note: to oust is to throw out, so the earl's letter is expelled

blocks.note: an inkling is a hint or clue
E is the abbreviation for earl
to broom is to sweep clear

explanation.surface: A hint makes a nobleman leave so the room can be cleared at a gentlemen's club.
explanation.walkthrough: The Athenaeum is an old gentlemen's club in London's Pall Mall.
explanation.definitionFit: A clubroom is the common room of a club, and the Athenaeum is one example of a club.

clue.text: Novice being unable to save most important board man?

blocks.note: being in a state is being in it

blocks.clueFragment: unable to save most important board man
blocks.note: when the king, the key chess piece, cannot be saved it is mate

explanation.surface: A beginner chess player cannot rescue the king.
explanation.walkthrough: A player who cannot save the king is 'in mate'. The novice is not a beginner but a member of a religious house.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice of a convent or monastery is one of its residents, and an inmate is anyone living within such an institution.

clue.text: Beastly group limited truck info

indicators.note: limited means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: Chambers gives truck in the sense of odd jobs, a chore
data and info both mean information

explanation.surface: A small lorry carries details about an animal herd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Truck' looks like a lorry; the setter uses a Chambers sense of small tasks.
explanation.definitionFit: Chordata is the animal phylum of creatures with a notochord, including all vertebrates.

clue.text: American spots fine vino but not dry sherry

indicators.note: but not means leaving out, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: taken as written; the sherry's letters come off both ends, so what is left also runs unbroken in the phrase, a coincidence of the subtraction rather than a hidden word
fino is a pale dry sherry

explanation.surface: An American picks out a good wine but not a dry sherry.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of the sherry are scattered through the phrase: f and i from fine, n and o from vino.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevi is the American spelling of naevi, plural of naevus, a birthmark or mole on the skin.

clue.text: Hold down hospital in order to take over in emergency

indicators.note: in means placed inside another word

blocks.note: to pin is to hold down
a chit is a written order or note
H is the abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Restraining a patient in hospital lets you seize control in a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinch-hit comes from baseball: batting in place of another player at a crucial moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinch-hit is to substitute for someone else, especially when urgently needed.

clue.text: I'm free! Triumphant expression in dock

indicators.note: in means placed inside another word

blocks.note: to dock is to cut short, or pare
olé is a cry of triumph

explanation.surface: A defendant cheers in the courtroom dock on being acquitted.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken by the answer: a released prisoner might shout it. 'Dock' looks like the courtroom, but it means to trim.
explanation.definitionFit: A parolee is a prisoner released early on parole, someone who could say they are free.

clue.text: Wine grape behind spending apparently

indicators.note: spending means using up and losing, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
ap. is an abbreviation of apparently
nache is an old word for the rump or buttocks

explanation.surface: A wine-grape variety seems to lag behind in spending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wine grape' looks like one definition; only 'Wine' is, and 'grape' is the start of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenache is a red wine made from the grape of that name, much grown in Spain and southern France.

clue.text: It receives and relays, eg, radio comedy bore

definitions.text: It receives and relays, eg, radio

blocks.note: com is a short form of comedy, as in romcom
bore as the past of bear, in the sense of sat or rested on

explanation.surface: A radio comedy show proves tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radio comedy' reads as one phrase; 'radio' belongs to the definition and 'bore' is a verb, not a dull person.
explanation.definitionFit: A comsat is a communications satellite, which picks up radio and TV signals and transmits them on.

clue.text: Surprised shriek over officer's decoration

blocks.note: o is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
the Distinguished Service Order is a medal for officers

explanation.surface: Someone yells in shock about an officer's medal.
explanation.definitionFit: Odso is an old exclamation of surprise, a mild oath found in older drama.

clue.text: Rule in the Orient, formerly but not now

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: the Orient is the East
r is a recognised abbreviation for rule

explanation.surface: An empire once governed the Far East but no longer does.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is doubly old: 'formerly' gives the meaning and 'but not now' flags that the word itself is obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Earst is an archaic form of erst, meaning at first or previously.

clue.text: Mean point that's not used now in curt speech

indicators.note: curt suggests cut short, so the word loses its final letter
in means one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: sides are an actor's lines, the speech an actor learns
ord is an obsolete word for a point

explanation.surface: A miserly person makes an outdated remark in brief words.
explanation.walkthrough: In the theatre, sides are the pages of a part given to an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Sordid and mean both describe something squalid, base and shabby.

clue.text: Brush totes vigorously (5, two words)

indicators.note: vigorously suggests shaken hard, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sweeps out some carrier bags with energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brush' is a skirmish, not a sweeping tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A brush is a short fight or skirmish, and a set-to is a brief scrap or argument.

clue.text: Get into what introduces synonym for benefactor

blocks.note: to don clothes is to get into them
or introduces an alternative name, as in 'the lexicon, or dictionary'

explanation.surface: A writer looks up how to bring in a synonym for patron.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor gives money or goods to a cause, as a benefactor does.

clue.text: Who goes downhill? Birthday dancer accepting end of trial run

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one piece holds the other
'end of' keeps only the last letter of 'trial'

blocks.note: Salome danced at Herod's birthday feast
the final letter of trial
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A dancer at a birthday party is going downhill after finishing a trial run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes downhill' sounds like declining; it is literal, on skis. In the Bible, Salome dances at Herod's birthday.
explanation.definitionFit: A slalomer is a skier racing down a winding course between gates.

clue.text: Bucks? Losers possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements of these letters

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Are dollars just losers' money, perhaps?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bucks' suggests dollars; it means male deer, and the question mark admits the answer is one particular kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorel is a buck fallow deer in its third year, so sorels are examples of bucks.

clue.text: Bleat about no good comic

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: maa is a goat's or sheep's bleat
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: Someone whines about a comedian who is useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic' looks like a comedian; it is a comic book.
explanation.definitionFit: Manga are Japanese comic books and graphic novels.

clue.text: Soldier I praise to cope with trial stoically (10, three words)

blocks.note: an old sweat is a veteran soldier
taken as written
to tout is to promote or praise

explanation.surface: A soldier says he praises those who bear a court case calmly.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweat it out is to endure an ordeal patiently until it ends.

clue.text: Annoy Republican departing with so much levy

indicators.note: departing means leaving, so that letter goes

blocks.note: to try someone's patience is to annoy them
R is the abbreviation for Republican
the means by so much, as in 'the more the merrier'

explanation.surface: A Republican annoyed by such a heavy tax walks out.
explanation.definitionFit: Tythe is an old spelling of tithe, a tax of a tenth paid to the church.

clue.text: In contact with parish church's chap in charge

blocks.note: as a door pulled to is in contact with its frame
par. is the abbreviation for parish
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A man running a church is in touch with the parish.
explanation.definitionFit: A toparch is the governor or ruler of a small district, so a man who is in charge.
